subject: Re: Brightline - request for temporary p95 relief and mitigation plan
messages:
From: Helen Park <hpark@brightline.tech>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API p95 spikes affecting checkout - request for short-term relief

Hi Vanessa,

We started seeing repeated p95 latency spikes in your hosted API this morning that are affecting our checkout flows (cart abandonment rising). Engineering has collected traces and attached a short CSV of request spikes and sample traces. These are concentrated between 08:40–09:00 PDT and appear correlated with a content-scan job that launched from our side — we think there were more large-context requests than usual.

We are on your standard hosted plan and understand the p50/p95 commitments, but given the customer impact we need either a temporary measurement accommodation or an emergency mitigation from Redwood so we can keep checkout online while we throttle the content-scan job.

Can you propose a concrete short-term plan (hours, not weeks) that gives us a stable p95 while we remediate on our side? We may need a written confirmation of the temporary change for our audit/procurement team.

Thanks — Helen
Helen Park
Head of Site Reliability, Brightline
attach: brightline-incident-log-20270718.csv (csv)
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Helen Park <hpark@brightline.tech>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API p95 spikes affecting checkout - request for short-term relief

Helen — thanks for the data, and sorry you hit this during a high-conversion window. I read the CSV and the pattern you described. We can help immediately; proposed approach below (short summary):

1) Temporary p95 variance window: grant a 72-hour temporary carveout window where we monitor but do not trigger SLA credits for p95 if the cause is a short-lived customer-side burst.
2) Active mitigations we can enact within 30–90 minutes:
   - Route Brightline traffic to an isolated soft pool (best-effort dedicated workers) so noisy bursts don’t impact the global hosted pool.
   - Turn on prefix-KV caching for repeated prompt prefixes in your workload.
   - Apply transient throttling/burst smoothing at edge for large-context jobs (we will keep per-token throughput limits conservative).
3) Measurement and audit: we will export evidence (request traces and percentile windows) and provide a signed addendum for your procurement team.
4) Rollback and guardrails: if we see sustained degradation beyond the 72 hours we will revert to previous routing and engage a joint remediation runbook.

I’m looping in Karthik and Ben for technical feasibility and an ETA for the routing/caching switch. I can produce a 1-page signed confirmation for procurement once we align on precise wording.

Next steps: Karthik / Ben please confirm we can spin the soft pool and enable prefix cache for Brightline within 90 minutes, and confirm any limits on request size we should apply. I’ll reply to Helen with an explicit timeline and the confirmation doc.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attach: brightline-temporary-slo-mitigation-plan-vanessa.pdf (pdf)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 09:51:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API p95 spikes affecting checkout - request for short-term relief

Vanessa — technically feasible. Notes & constraints:

- Soft pool routing: we can create an account-scoped soft pool that pins Brightline traffic to a capped set of instances. This isolates noisy neighbors. ETA: 45–75 minutes depending on queueing. Works for hosted API; no customer infra changes required.
- Prefix KV cache: low-friction, but effectiveness depends on prompt repeatability. We’ll enable a conservative TTL and collect hit-rate metrics.
- Edge throttling: we can enforce a per-request token ceiling for this account (e.g. 4k token cap) as an emergency measure. Some checkout flows may need larger contexts; we should validate.
- Measurement: Important to be explicit on the measurement window. For this temporary accommodation we suggest:
   * Keep p50 as-is.
   * For p95, do a 72-hour conditional non-credit window bounded by the specific incident times (start time = 2027-07-18T09:34:00-07:00).
   * Export rolling 1-minute quantiles and per-route trace samples for audit.

I will spin up the soft pool and enable the cache. I’ll also start a brief canary (5% of traffic) to validate no downstream regressions. I’ll update this thread when the soft pool is live.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Helen Park <hpark@brightline.tech>, Procurement <procure@brightline.tech>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed short-term SLO variance and next steps (Brightline)

Helen / Procurement — per Karthik’s note, we can act immediately. Concretely:

- Effective immediately we will:
  1) Create an account-scoped soft pool for Brightline (isolation) — expected live ETA 70 minutes.
  2) Enable prefix-KV caching for your primary routes.
  3) Apply a temporary per-request token ceiling of 4,096 tokens for the affected routes; we can raise for specific flows if you confirm.

- Measurement accommodation: Redwood will apply a conditional 72-hour p95 non-credit window starting now. During that window we will still collect full telemetry and supply an evidence package (traces, 1-minute quantiles, per-route traffic summary) for your audit. If the anomaly is classified as customer-side burst and our mitigations stabilize metrics, no SLA credits will be processed for this window.

- Paperwork: I’ve generated a one-page addendum that states the temporary variance and the mitigation steps. You can sign via DocuSign here: https://www.docusign.com/brightline/slo-variance. If procurement needs any different wording, send a suggested clause and we’ll incorporate it.

- Monitoring & rollback: We will run a 5% canary for 30 minutes after the pool is live and escalate if errors or global impact is detected. If everything looks green we will keep mitigation in place for up to 72 hours while you remediate.

Can you confirm acceptance so Ben/Karthik can proceed? Also confirm whether any checkout flows need >4,096 tokens so we can make exceptions.

Thanks,
—Vanessa
From: Helen Park <hpark@brightline.tech>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procure@brightline.tech>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed short-term SLO variance and next steps (Brightline)

Vanessa — thank you, that plan works for us. We accept the 72-hour conditional variance and Ben’s mitigations. Procurement will review the one-page addendum and sign via DocuSign; you should see the envelope shortly. We’ll also throttle the content-scan job immediately and validate checkout flows against the 4,096 token ceiling.

Please proceed with the soft pool and the canary. If anything changes we’ll notify you.

—Helen
